exposure: Grades of Meconium Stained Amniotic Fluid (MSAF) (Thin MSAF, Thick MSAF)
cohort: The study included 126 subjects detected with Meconium Stained Amniotic Fluid (MSAF) after spontaneous or artificial rupture of membranes.
finding: Thick MSAF was significantly associated with abnormal cord blood parameters (high lactate, low pH), abnormal fetal heart rate patterns, increased rates of LSCS, lower APGAR scores, increased need for resuscitation, higher NICU admission rates, and development of Meconium Aspiration Syndrome, indicative of poor perinatal and neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Subjects with thick MSAF had increased rates of LSCS (80.25%), whereas the majority of subjects with thin MSAF delivered vaginally with good neonatal outcomes.
